title: Existence of normalized total derived module adjunction
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal C$ be small categories with Grothendieck topologies $K$ and $J$, let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be continuous, let $R$ and $S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on them, and let $a:R\to u_*S$ be a sheaf ring map. Suppose $u^{-1}$ on sheaves of sets preserves finite limits. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with chosen localization universes. For small sites and an arbitrary structural ring map represented by a continuous functor whose inverse image on sheaves of sets preserves finite limits, the module pullback and pushforward admit total derived functors, their universal transformations and an adjunction normalized on every chain map from a termwise pulled-back complex. The package is [def-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-data]. The left-derived transformation is invertible on every flat-term K-flat complex, as computed by the ringed-topos derived-pullback theorem.

proof.text: Use the continuous ringed-topos module direct-image presentation and its supplied K-flat pullback. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies that pullback with the canonical site pullback and transfers preservation of quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat complexes.

Flat-term K-flat resolutions give a resolving class in the homotopy category. Construct the total left derived functor and its comparison, invertible on that class. Fullness and object-surjectivity of the homotopy quotient transfer its universal property to complexes. K-injective derivability supplies the right derived functor and its comparison.

Resolving-class essential constancy gives absolute pro-diagram limits, so postcomposition by the right derived functor preserves the left-derived universal property. The K-injective good-object criterion likewise proves that postcomposition of the right derived functor by the left derived functor remains right derived. Apply Mathlib Adjunction.derived. Its unit factorization and naturality of the right-derived comparison prove the normalized Hom formula. The resolving-class comparison computes on flat-term K-flat complexes.
